reviews.title: Money hungry monster who won’t let me sing
reviews.text:
I downloaded Simply Sing because I wanted to practice singing and have fun, but I was really disappointed. So many features seem locked behind a subscription, and it feels like the app keeps pushing you to pay before you can properly use it. I expected to be able to sing more songs without constantly running into paywalls.

The app itself works okay, but the free version feels very limited. If you’re looking for an app that lets you sing freely without spending money, this might not be the best choice.

I ended up uninstalling it because I felt like I couldn’t actually enjoy singing without being asked to subscribe all the time. Hopefully the developers make more content available for free in the future.

“User generated content. We may also collect content you provide to us when you use our Services, such as information regarding your use of the Services, sample audio recordings for quality assurance and improving acoustic recognition experience, and other information relevant to customer surveys and/or commercial offers. We store all messages sent to our forums to help users find useful information about the Services.”

reviews.title: Completely Misleading – No Free Trial, No Real Access
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app because it looked interesting and I wanted to genuinely try it out. They walk you through finding your vocal range, which makes it seem like you’re about to actually use the features — but then the second you try to test a song, you’re hit with a paywall. You literally can’t try the core feature without paying first. How is anyone supposed to know if they like it?
Honestly, that feels like a scam. You’re promoting an app with someone freely testing songs and using all the features, but real users can’t even try one song without committing to $60 a year or $15 a month. That’s completely misleading. It gives the impression you can actually experience the app before paying, when you absolutely cannot.
There should 100% be a free trial or at least a limited number of free songs. Promoting it the way they do, knowing users can’t actually test it like the person in the ad, is deceptive. Total waste of time. I’ll be deleting it. Ridiculous and disappointing.

reviews.title: Rubbish, I mean RUBBISH!
reviews.text:
So.. with this app, the testing lets you scream and shout like a loony at your phone for a few minutes, then comes back to say, in my case, you’re a Tenor.. well, who knew!! But then the app will then change all their music to align with your range. Not only will you never sing with your favourite artist, or in place of them, as your favourite artist may not even be there no matter how globally well known they are. I suspect they may have seen this app and said No, quite categorically and simply…no way! To sing and test your vocals with the newly ranged music of your second or third (maybe 12th) fave music star, you have to subscribe, and it ain’t cheap! 

So no, I’d rather harass and frighten the life out of my dog and the wildlife while screeching like a cat on a creaky door in my shower, with ears full of soap suds!! 

I’ll give this a miss and remain in my delusional world, of some music guru passing my bathroom window to only fall in love with my dodgy vocals and dulcet tones. Although, questions may be asked why they were trespassing on private property. 

I’d rather spend my money on another album of my fave singer so I may crucify the lyrics my own special way. 

Seriously, buy an album or sing a jingle and live your dream… there’s always X-Factor to really slap your delusional dreams down. 

Oh and for the record, no, I won’t benefit from subscribing to any length of subscription by paying a fee. I’m off to buy several albums, thank you very much!!
